name: call_frames_v1
spec: CIRISServer 0.5.246 call frames socket, WS /v1/chat/{room}/call/frames; one WebSocket binary message = one frame; integers big-endian. Agreed with CIRISClient CSD-134 (PR #287) and CIRISEdge.

layout.client_to_node: ver u8 (=1) | codec_id u8 | spatial u8 | temporal u8 | quality u8 | payload...
layout.node_to_client: ver u8 (=1) | codec_id u8 | spatial u8 | temporal u8 | quality u8 | pub_len u16 | publisher[pub_len] UTF-8 key_id | stream_id[32] | epoch u64 | chunk_seq u64 | source_ts_ms u64 | flags u8 (bit 0: frame_seq present; others reserved, 0) | frame_seq u32 (0 when absent) | payload...

notes: Audio: codec_id 0xFF (edge CODEC_OPAQUE), layer (0,0,0), payload = exactly one Opus packet (RFC 6716), 48 kHz mono, 20 ms, VBR, VOIP application, 24-32 kbit/s. No inner header; no DTX or FEC in v1; the app does PLC.

Video: codec_id is passed through. Valid ids every client handles: 0xFF (audio, opaque), 0x01 (AV1 SVC) and, SHOULD, 0x04 (H.264, temporal-layered, spatial 0; CC). The stream's binding names the codec. Frames v1 enforces only the opaque base-layer rule.
codec_id 0xFF with a layer other than (0,0,0) is refused (edge requires the base cell for opaque chunks).
publisher is at most 256 bytes. A payload over the call's frame_budget_bytes is refused with a text event, never cut; that check is the route's, not the codec's.
The opus vector payload is a real 60-byte packet: TOC 0x78 (hybrid full-band, mono, one 20 ms frame), a 440 Hz tone encoded by libopus.

Video payloads (CSD-134): 0x04 H.264 = one access unit in Annex B with SPS/PPS before every keyframe; 0x01 AV1 = one temporal unit's low-overhead OBUs for that layer (obu_has_size_field=1) with the sequence header OBU before every keyframe.

source_ts_ms is the publisher's signed capture time (ms since the Unix epoch), for lip sync. frame_seq is present on video and other non-audio frames and absent on audio (Eric via edge v45, 2026-11-10). It counts per (stream, codec class, layer), the layer being the full (spatial, temporal, quality) triple: each layer's frame of a picture carries that layer's own counter, the base layer advances once per picture that has a base frame, an enhancement layer only on pictures that carry it, and every fragment of one frame carries the same value. It runs for the stream's life (no restart at an epoch roll); a replaced stream starts again at 0. Compare it only between frames of the same layer: a base-layer gap means hold until the next keyframe; an enhancement-layer gap means decode at the lower layer until that layer's next decodable point; layers not being received are never a gap.

client_to_node.name: video_h264_keyframe
client_to_node.note: A real H.264 keyframe access unit (Annex B, SPS + PPS + IDR; libx264 baseline 32x32 4:2:0 testsrc), as CSD-134 fixes the 0x04 payload. Decodable on its own; 663 B is over a 244 B v44 budget, which is the route's refusal, not the codec's.

events.encoding: one JSON object per WebSocket text message; member = a key_id, never a name; every stream_id = 64 lowercase hex, the binary frame's raw 32 bytes; an event naming a member also carries `person` (the node's owner, null until bound); `ready.fragmenting` says whether the node splits an over-budget frame (edge 45.1) or refuses it

examples.reason: the room's epoch could not be followed

events.notes: Edge v45.0.0 (0.5.246). attendee_left with stream_id carries the attendee's signed cause (CallEvent::AttendeeLeft): left|backgrounded from its signed end, removed when its key left the room's MLS group, lost when every leg went and its stream stayed silent 5 s. attendee_left without stream_id is the room dropping a member (CallEvent::MemberLeft, left=removed); a client may see both for one person and treats leaving as idempotent. stream_added.kind is media|share (CC rc18; an unknown value renders as media). stream_ended.ended adds `ended` (a share stopped, the attendee stays). stream_replaced: new_stream_id carries on old_stream_id, with no leave. video_unavailable: this node hears that member only through the canonical, audio only; video_restored when a member path carries it again. video_allowed: sent on connect and on change; above max_people the call is audio only and video frames are refused (publish_refused video_two_people_only). Screen share is refused (call.share_unavailable) until 45.1. Edge 45.2.0 (CIRISServer 0.5.254; edge docs/calls_relay_tokens.md, frozen for 45.x, unknown tokens show as the generic case): relay_status.relaying_for counts PEOPLE (the server maps edge's child nodes to owners; an unbound node is one person), relaying_for_nodes is edge's node count, serve_seat true means no relay switch. media_path_restored.through is a node key id (the attendee member id space), null on a direct path; direct = via != peer_relay. media_path_failed.cause and .relay are edge tokens verbatim with reason_id call.media_path_failed.<cause> and relay_reason_id call.relay_standing.<relay>; diag is edge's serde form, for the ? panel only. call_ended: the call ended under the socket; ended is edge's token, reason_id from call_ended_values (a mid-call media refusal reuses the join refusal's id); the node then closes the socket with the bare token as the close reason. Join refusals: call.anonymous_mode (token onion_anonymous_no_media) and call.shaped_only (token shaped_only_no_media). call_ended ended=call_full (reason_id call.full, with max_people and people) is the server's own: a call holds at most four people on edge 45.2.0; a device whose join made it five leaves within 30 s of joining, and a join that already sees five is refused 409 call.full. The members who were there first stay; a room still seats six. Server 0.5.255: `connecting {members, since_ms, reach}` is sent when the socket opens and once more if no `ready` came within 20 s; members are the room's other PEOPLE (room members are person keys; each reach entry lists that person's nodes held here, a person with two devices is one entry with two nodes), since_ms the unix ms the socket opened. reach is THIS node's view: last_heard_ms_ago = age of the newest row held here that the person or one of their nodes signed (null: none); reachable_now is null (unknown) until edge 45.3 peer_reach. A warning, never a refusal. The join answer and GET call state carry the same `reach`; call_id is 64 lowercase hex; service_tier is edge's token load_tier:0|1|2; state is {state: live} | {state: degraded, epoch, reason} | {state: ended, ended, reason_id}; frame_budget_bytes is null until a leg is up.

alert.default: ring when the room has at most 4 people (CALL_MAX_PEOPLE), notify above that
alert.join_answer: `alert`: the mode used, when this join opened the call; null when it joined a call already live (that alerts nobody)
alert.meaning: open: the call is just there (members see it from the call row). notify: each other person's nodes get call_notice, with no ring, no decline and no timeout; the caller's socket gets notified {members}. ring: everything below. Eric 2026-11-27: ringing is a choice, e.g. a live chat in a room of 100. The opener sets it; a receiver may only lower it for itself. Carried in the ring message until edge's call row has the member (after 45.3).

ringing.spec: Server 0.5.255 (src/call_ring.rs). Transient call control, never a row: nothing is stored or replicated, a ring reaches only the nodes of the room's other people, a receiver refuses a non-member (403) and more than 6 rings a minute from one key (429). A call joined with nobody else in it rings every node of every other person in the room (never the caller's own other devices). It rings while the app runs; a backgrounded phone is not woken (CIRISServer#24).

node_events.stream: GET /v1/calls/events (SSE, the owner's session). Opens with event `ringing_now` = GET /v1/calls/ringing's body; then one event per ring change, the SSE event name = `type`; `resync` {fetch} after a lag.

ringing.notes: `ringing` is sent once every member node has answered the ring or failed to (unreachable = no path now or no answer within 8 s; refused = the member's node refused it, e.g. it doesn't hold that room yet; in_call = that node is already in this room's call, two people having joined at once, and it was not rung). `no_answer` why=declined when every member rung declined or is busy (the call stays up; the caller leaves); why=timeout after 45 s with nobody joined, and then the node sends call_ended {ended: no_answer, reason_id: call.no_answer} and leaves the call itself; the socket closes. Someone joining ends the ring everywhere: their own other devices hear answered_elsewhere. Answering is joining the call (POST /v1/chat/{room}/call); it stops this device ringing.
